items.summaryZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳暗示，被认为对车队影响过大导致他去年离开红牛F1车队主管职位。

items.originalTitle: Christian Horner opens up on Red Bull F1 exit: “Perhaps it was perceived I had too much influence over the team”
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳在谈到红牛一级方程式车队离职时表示：“或许人们觉得我对车队的影响太大”
克里斯蒂安·霍纳就为什么红牛去年决定与他分手发表了看法
克里斯蒂安·霍纳暗示，人们觉得他对车队的影响太大，这导致了他去年作为红牛一级方程式车队主管的离职
这位前红牛老板监督了车队转变为能量饮料品牌车队，并进入了两个一级方程式统治时代：首先是与塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔一起，在2010-13年间获得了四个一级方程式世界车手和世界车队制造商的冠军，然后是与马克斯·维斯塔潘一起，在2021-24年间获得了四个世界车手冠军和三个世界车队制造商的冠军。
但是，在针对不当行为指控的内部调查和上诉——这两者都清除了霍纳的名誉——的过程中，2024年在红牛内部引发了一场激烈的权力斗争。
随着像阿德里安·纽维和乔纳森·惠特利这样的高知名度团队成员离职，以及红牛在2025年的成绩下滑，霍纳在2025年7月被解除了车队主管的职务。
在接受姐妹杂志《AutoSport》的独家采访时，霍纳谈到了他认为导致他离职的原因。
“我认为公司只是想要走向不同的方向，或者可能有人觉得我对车队的影响太大，”霍纳说。“当然，迪特里希[马特希奇]去世后的生活，在集团内部已经大不相同了。”
霍纳被红牛联合创始人迪特里希·马特希奇选中，领导F1车队在收购捷豹车队后的转型，并在他们的合作中一直是亲密的盟友。
2022年10月马特希奇的去世普遍被认为引发了红牛车队的权力斗争，品牌董事会，在首席执行官奥利弗·明茨拉夫的监督下，寻求在F1运营上获得更多控制权，并远离霍纳的职责范围。
霍纳向马特希奇以及他在红牛对他的信任表示敬意。
“他是红牛。所有重要的决定都经过他，他与Yoovidhya家族在伟大的合作中从无到有地建立了这个业务，”霍纳说，指的是马特希奇以外的红牛其他联合拥有者。
“迪特里希对赛车、汽车充满热情，他热爱车手，热爱所有形式的赛车运动。当你看到他所做出的贡献，不仅仅是对于一级方程式，还有拉力赛，以及所有青训车队，你今天看到的任何形式的赛车运动，都不难发现太阳和公牛标志以某种方式出现在车辆或车手身上。”
“很容易低估他为赛车运动世界所做的一切，因此，不可避免地，当你失去这样一个创始人时，留下的是一个空缺，一切都变得不同。他对我很不错，给了我机会，他信任我，并给了我运营业务的自由，我将永远感激他。”
“红牛帝国最高层的这种地震级变化震撼了整个组织，霍纳觉得这对他作为红牛一级方程式车队主管的角色产生了影响。”
“在那之后，一切都变得不同了。突然之间，委员会和公司驱动的[管理]比以前一个创始人一个人管理要多得多，决策过程也与我们习惯的不同。”
您可以在这里观看与克里斯蒂安·霍纳的《Autosport访谈》完整内容。
detailEn: Christian Horner opens up on Red Bull F1 exit: “Perhaps it was perceived I had too much influence over the team”
Christian Horner gives his opinion on why Red Bull decided to part company with him last year
Christian Horner has hinted that “it was perceived that I had too much influence over the team” which led to his departure as Red Bull Formula 1 team principal last year.

The former Red Bull boss oversaw the team’s transformation into the energy drinks-branded outfit and into two eras of F1 domination: firstly with Sebastian Vettel and four consecutive F1 world drivers’ and world constructors’ titles between 2010-13 and then with Max Verstappen with four world drivers’ championships and three world constructors’ crowns between 2021-24.
But amid an internal investigation over allegations of inappropriate behaviour and an appeal – both of which cleared Horner’s name – it set into action a fractious power struggle at Red Bull in 2024.
With high profile team members such as Adrian Newey and Jonathan Wheatley leaving and Red Bull’s results in decline going into 2025, Horner was sacked as team principal in July 2025.
In an exclusive interview with sister publication Autosport, Horner has opened up on what he felt led to his departure.

“I think the company just wanted to go in a different direction, or perhaps it was perceived I had too much influence over the team,” Horner said. “And, of course, life after Dietrich [Mateschitz] had passed was quite different within the group.”
Horner was chosen by Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz to lead the transformation of the F1 team following the takeover of the Jaguar outfit, and was a close ally throughout their partnership.

Mateschitz’s death in October 2022 is widely considered to have started the power struggle at the Red Bull team, with the brand’s board, overseen by CEO Oliver Mintzlaff, looking to take more control over F1 operations and away from Horner’s remit.
Horner paid tribute to Mateschitz and the faith he put in him at Red Bull.

“He was Red Bull. All the significant decisions were going through him, he built that business from nothing in a great partnership with the Yoovidhya family,” Horner said, referring to Red Bull’s other co-owners alongside Mateschitz.

“Dietrich was passionate about racing, cars, he loved the drivers, he loved all forms of motorsport. When you look at the contribution he made, not just to Formula 1 but to rallying, to all the junior categories, there's not a form of motorsport that you look at these days that doesn't in some way have the sun and bull logo on a car or on a driver.

“It's easy to underestimate what he actually has done for the world of motorsport, so inevitably when you lose a founder like that it leaves a void and it's just different. He was very good to me, he gave me the chance, he believed in me and he gave me the freedom to operate the business and I'll forever be grateful to him for that.”
It was this seismic change at the very top of the Red Bull empire that shook up the organisation and Horner felt it had an impact on his role at Red Bull F1 team principal.

“It was just different after that. Suddenly there was a lot more committee and corporately-driven [management] than perhaps a one-man founder and the decision-making process that we'd become accustomed to.”
You can watch 'The Autosport Interview' with Christian Horner in its entirety here.

items.originalTitle: Valentino Rossi wary of Max Verstappen threat at Portimao: "Big problem"
items.summaryEn: Max Verstappen makes his GT World Challenge Europe debut at the Portimao season finale this weekend, and MotoGP legend Valentino Rossi will also be racing, with both wary of meeting each other during the race.
detailZh: 瓦伦蒂诺·罗西警惕波尔蒂芒的马克斯·维斯塔潘威胁：“大问题”
这位MotoGP传奇将在阿尔加维赛道的顶级Pro组别中与维斯塔潘同场竞技。
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察和比赛分析。
两位赛车运动中最著名的车手本周末即将共享发车格，而且他们都对比赛中相遇非常警惕。马克斯·维斯塔潘本周末在波尔蒂芒的赛季收官战中完成GT世界挑战赛欧洲杯首秀，但他将要竞争的60多辆赛车中，有一辆将由MotoGP传奇瓦伦蒂诺·罗西驾驶。这位九届摩托车世界冠军已与意大利天空体育讨论了他对与F1最伟大车手之一对决的感受。
“这将会非常精彩。我的意思是，这会是个大麻烦，因为他肯定会快得惊人，但这也会非常棒，”他说。
“我得说，我从没想过自己会朝着马克斯·维斯塔潘的方向比赛。所以这很棒，有他在那里对每个人来说都会很棒，我希望我能有机会跟在他后面，看看他是怎么开车的。”
这是一个清楚知道自己面对的是什么，并且很兴奋能把它当作学习机会的人。
维斯塔潘将驾驶维斯塔潘车队的3号梅赛德斯-AMG GT3 EVO赛车。他和他的搭档车手克里斯·卢勒姆以及雷克萨斯厂队车手本·巴尼科特将参加最高级别的Pro组。他将在红牛车队于新加坡和马来西亚连续两场获胜后抵达赛道。
罗西将代表WRT车队参加Pro组别，驾驶一辆宝马M4 GT3 EVO，队友是尼尔·维哈根和马克斯·赫塞。他会使用自己惯用的46号。这辆车属于同一组别，所以他们在激烈驾驶时很可能会相遇。
“是的，我希望我能见到他，”维斯塔潘说。“他是个非常酷的人，所以我希望能和他叙叙旧。我的意思是，这很好，但我不希望在比赛中见到他，所以这通常是个好兆头。
“其实我希望谁都见不到，就自己在前面跑，做好自己的工作。但你永远不知道会发生什么。发车区竞争超级激烈，所以我只是期待这个挑战。
“这和一级方程式非常不同，但我喜欢。我的意思是，今年我在纽博格林北环赛道已经第一次体验过了，而波尔蒂芒是一条开起来非常酷的赛道。所以我会好好享受，当然，作为一支车队，我们会尽力争取一个好成绩。”
这场三小时的比赛将于10月17日星期六举行，地点是4.692公里（2.9英里）的阿尔加维赛道，该赛道曾在2020年和2021年举办过葡萄牙大奖赛。
detailEn: Valentino Rossi wary of Max Verstappen threat at Portimao: "Big problem"
The MotoGP legend will race Verstappen in the top Pro class at the Algarve circuit
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Two of motorsport's biggest drivers are about to share a grid this weekend, and they're both very wary of meeting each other during the race. Max Verstappen makes his GT World Challenge Europe debut at the Portimao season finale this weekend, but one of the 60-odd cars he will be racing will be driven by MotoGP legend Valentino Rossi. The nine-time motorcycle world champion has discussed with Sky Sport Italy how he feels about going up against the one of Formula 1's greatest drivers.
"It's going to be amazing. I mean, it will be a big problem because he’s sure to be incredibly fast, but it will be fantastic," he said.
"I have to say, I never imagined I’d be racing towards Max Verstappen. So it’s great, it’ll be great for everyone to have him there, and I hope I get the chance to follow him and see how he drives."
That is a man who knows exactly what he's up against, and is excited to use it as a learning moment.

Verstappen will be driving the #3 Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO for Verstappen Racing. He and his co-drivers Chris Lulham and Lexus factory driver Ben Barnicoat will be running in the top Pro class. He'll arrive at the track following two consecutive wins with Red Bull in Singapore and Malaysia.

Rossi will be driving a BMW M4 GT3 EVO in the Pro class with Team WRT alongside Neil Verhagen and Max Hesse. He'll be using his usual #46. This car is in the same category, so it's likely they will indeed meet each other while driving in anger.
"Yeah, I hope I get to see him," Verstappen said. "He’s a very cool guy, so I hope to catch up with him. I mean, it’s nice, but I do not hope to see him in the race, so that’s normally a good sign.
"I actually hope to see no one, to be just up front and do a good job. But you never know. The grid is super competitive, so I’m just looking forward to the challenge.

"It’s very different to Formula 1, but I love it. I mean, I had my first taste already this year at the Nordschleife, and Portimao is a very cool track to drive. So I’m just going to enjoy it and, of course, as a team, we’ll try to do the best we can to get a good result out of it."
The three-hour race takes place Saturday, 17 October, on the 4.692 km (2.9 miles) Algarve circuit that hosted the Portuguese Grand Prix in 2020 and 2021.

detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳透露F1生涯中的恐慌症斗争
克里斯蒂安·霍纳感谢医生帮助他在多年的F1维修区压力下识别浅呼吸和焦虑
克里斯蒂安·霍纳，红牛车队车队负责人
对于红牛车迷来说，关注红牛车队，了解F1新闻、车手更新、技术洞察和米尔顿凯恩斯的比赛分析
在光鲜的维修区围板、领奖台香槟和不懈的政治操纵背后，一级方程式赛车运动对那些驾驶着数百万美元操作的个体施加了残酷、往往看不见的代价。二十年来，克里斯蒂安·霍纳作为红牛车队的领军人物，展现出了坚定不移的外表，在激烈的冠军争夺战和残酷的赛道战争中保持着绝对的冷静。
然而，在与《卫报》的一次深刻对话中，这位52岁的前车队负责人揭开了他幕后所承受的严重生理压力的序幕，详细描述了慢性压力最终如何导致可怕的恐慌发作。
误将恐慌发作归咎于'喝太多咖啡'
管理一支赢得冠军的车队，跨越繁忙的赛历，其不懈的要求最终对身心造成了实际的损害。霍纳回忆起他经历了令人担忧的心血管和呼吸系统症状，他最初试图将这些症状归咎于常规疲劳或咖啡因摄入过多。
“我不知道那是什么，”霍纳在描述攻击开始时承认道，“你突然感到头晕，对呼吸变得敏感，你觉得有些奇怪的事情正在发生。我把它归咎于在一个压抑、闷热、雷雨交加的日子里喝太多咖啡。”
红牛车队车队经理克里斯蒂安·霍纳
当这些情况再次发生时，霍纳寻求了医学评估，结果发现根本原因不是身体疾病，而是心理过载。
“然后它又发生了。我进行了检查，但身体上没有任何问题，”霍纳透露，“他们说，'我们认为你有焦虑症。你的呼吸非常浅。'这是我的身体在告诉我，你在这里的压力很大。我现在能够识别这些症状并让它过去，然后呼吸。”
“身份”的空虚和对Toto Wolff的赞扬
在2025年7月意外离开红牛车队后，压力的生理表现最终被突如其来的身份真空所加剧。在米尔顿凯恩斯担任了20年的核心决策者，突然被从这个充满活力的环境中移除，引发了一段深刻的自我反思时期。
在反思心理冲击时，霍纳意外地对他最激烈的职业对手、梅赛德斯车队负责人Toto Wolff表示敬意，Wolff曾公开谈论自己与临床抑郁症和治疗的经历。
“Toto公开谈论我们这个年龄段的人可能会遇到的问题非常勇敢，”霍纳承认。“我虽然没有经历过这些问题，但在这个时期我对人们是如何[受苦的]有了更深的理解。”
Christian Horner，红牛车队负责人，Toto Wolff，梅赛德斯-AMG车队负责人兼首席执行官
Horner强调，当表现优异的专业人士突然失去职业目标时，心理上的影响可能是毁灭性的。
“许多中年人的身份是通过他们的工作来定义的。突然间，你失去了这一切，”Horner解释道。“你是谁？你是什么？你的目标是什么？你要么蜷缩成一团，要么振作起来站起来。”
尽管Horner坚持认为一级方程式赛车仍然是激发他职业热情的主要领域，但离开赛道为他提供了一个前所未有的生活方式的重置。在连续21个赛季中错过了无数个人里程碑之后，Horner得以在伦敦度过赛车周末，庆祝女儿Olivia的13岁生日，带她去西区观看音乐剧《汉密尔顿》
询问他真正怀念体育运动的哪些元素时，霍纳毫不犹豫地指出了界限。
"人、团队、竞争。我仍然热爱这项运动，" 霍纳总结道。"但我并不怀念旅行和政治。"
detailEn: Christian Horner reveals secret battle with panic attacks during F1 career
Christian Horner credits doctors with helping him recognise shallow breathing and anxiety after years of F1 pitwall stress
Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Behind the polished pitwall pitboards, podium champagne, and relentless political maneuvering, Formula 1 extracts a grueling, often invisible toll on the individuals steering its multi-million-dollar operations. For two decades, Christian Horner presented an unflappable exterior as Red Bull Racing's figurehead, projecting absolute composure across intense title showdowns and bitter paddock wars.

However, in a deeply revealing conversation with The Guardian, the 52-year-old former team principal pulled back the curtain on the severe physiological distress he weathered behind the scenes, detailing how chronic stress eventually culminated in terrifying panic attacks.
Mistaking panic attacks for 'too much coffee'

The relentless demands of managing a championship-winning team across a sprawling calendar eventually took a tangible physical toll. Horner recalled experiencing alarming cardiovascular and respiratory episodes, which he initially tried to dismiss as routine fatigue or excessive caffeine intake.

"I didn't know what it was," Horner admitted when describing the onset of the attacks. "You suddenly feel dizzy and conscious of your breathing, and you think there's something strange going on. I put it down to having had too much coffee on an oppressive, muggy, thundery day."
Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing
When the episodes recurred, Horner sought medical evaluation, only to find that the root cause was psychological overload rather than a somatic illness.

"Then it happened again. I got checked out, and there was nothing physically the matter," Horner revealed. "They said, 'We think you have anxiety. Your breathing's very shallow.' It was my body telling me you're pushing pretty hard here. I'm able to recognise the symptoms now and let it go, and breathe."
The "identity" void and praising Toto Wolff

The physical manifestations of stress were eventually compounded by an abrupt identity vacuum following his unexpected departure from Red Bull in July 2025. After spending 20 years as the central decision-maker in Milton Keynes, being suddenly removed from that high-octane environment triggered a period of profound existential reflection.

Reflecting on the psychological shock, Horner paid unexpected tribute to his fiercest career rival, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, who has spoken publicly about his own history with clinical depression and therapy.

"Toto was very brave to talk openly about such a factor for people our age," Horner acknowledged. "I hadn't experienced those issues, but I had an appreciation during this period of how people could [suffer]."
Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing, Toto Wolff, Team Principal and CEO, Mercedes AMG
Horner emphasised that when high-performing professionals have their vocational purpose abruptly severed, the psychological fallout can be devastating.

"The identity of many middle-aged guys is through their work. Suddenly you have that stripped and taken from you," Horner explained. "Who are you? What are you? What is your purpose? You either curl up into a ball or brush yourself down and get up."

While Horner maintains that Formula 1 remains the primary arena that excites him professionally, stepping away from the paddock has provided an unprecedented lifestyle reset. After missing countless personal milestones over 21 consecutive seasons, Horner was able to spend race weekend in London celebrating his daughter Olivia's 13th birthday, taking her to the West End to watch the musical Hamilton.
Asked what elements of the sport he genuinely misses, Horner was unequivocal about where the line is drawn.
"The people, the team, the competition. I still love the sport," Horner concluded. "But I don't miss the travel and politics."
